name: TeamRetro: Park lost HubSpot deals as win/loss retro prompts

parameters.content:
## TeamRetro: Park lost HubSpot deals as win/loss retro prompts

### How it works

When a HubSpot deal moves to closed-lost, the workflow fetches the deal, skips anything under a value floor, and asks one OpenAI call to turn the loss notes into at most two discussion prompts. CRM notes are attributed and blamey — "rep missed the demo", "champion went dark" — so parking them verbatim turns the retro into a blame session. The system prompt forces neutral questions about process, product, pricing or market instead, and that transform is the point of this template. Surviving prompts are checked by word overlap against the last 30 days of parked items, parked in TeamRetro for the sales team's win/loss retro, then logged back on the deal timeline.

### Setup steps

- **Map your own closed-lost stage ID in "Closed Lost?".** The default pipeline uses `closedlost`, but a custom or renamed stage gets a different internal ID, often numeric. Find yours under HubSpot → Settings → Objects → Deals → Pipelines.
- Two HubSpot credentials: a developer app for the trigger, a private app token with `crm.objects.deals.read` and `write` for the deal nodes.
- Add an OpenAI credential to "OpenAI GPT-5 Mini", then replace `REPLACE_WITH_TEAM_ID` on both TeamRetro nodes. The parking lot is a plan feature — a 403 means it is not on your plan.
- Sample data is pinned on the trigger and "Get Deal", so Execute workflow replays a lost deal before you connect HubSpot.

### Customization

`minDealAmount` in "Extract Deal Facts" is the floor (default 5000, deal currency) — set it to 0 to park every loss. `THRESHOLD` in "Token-Overlap Dedupe" tunes duplicate sensitivity. For the win side, duplicate the branch on your closed-won stage and reframe the prompt.

## 1. Catch the closed-lost deal

The trigger fires on every deal stage change. **Stage IDs differ per portal** — put your own closed-lost internal ID into "Closed Lost?" or nothing will ever pass this gate.

## 2. Skip the small losses

`minDealAmount` in "Extract Deal Facts" is the floor. A deal with no amount counts as zero and is skipped.

## 3. Draft blameless prompts

One call returns `parkable` plus at most two prompts of 90 characters or less. Unparkable losses end the run quietly. Swap the model sub-node for Anthropic, Gemini or Ollama.

## 4. Dedupe against the parking lot

The third "we keep losing on SSO" deal should not become a third parked item. `THRESHOLD` tunes how aggressively word overlap treats a rewording as a duplicate.

## 5. Park it and close the loop

`title` is the only field the parked-item API accepts, so the deal name rides inside it. A completed activity lands back on the deal timeline.

messageValues.message:
You prepare discussion prompts for a sales team's win/loss retrospective. Given one closed-lost deal, return exactly:
- parkable: true only if the loss data contains something the team could learn from or discuss. False when there is no loss reason and no notes, or the deal looks like a test, import artifact, or duplicate.
- prompts: at most TWO discussion prompts, each a single neutral sentence or question of maximum 90 characters.

Prompts must be blameless: ask about process, product, pricing, or market — never about a named person, and never assign fault. Rephrase "the rep missed the demo" as "How might we make demo scheduling more resilient?". Never include people's names, customer contact details, or deal amounts in the prompts. If parkable is false, return an empty prompts array.

description.value: Champion went quiet after the security review. Procurement had accepted pricing — the gap was product (no SAML SSO) and onboarding speed. Competitor demoed a two-week rollout; our standard plan quotes five.
